subject: Dashboard sweeps + cost-anomaly playbook request
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@datacalyx.com
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dashboard sweeps + cost-anomaly playbook request

Team —

We had Calyx (ops@datacalyx.com) flag a sequence of cost spikes on two public routes this weekend; their account saw a 3x token spend change with only a small increase in qps. They asked for a per-route breakdown and a repeatable investigation/playbook we can run and hand to CSMs.

Ask: can Console provide the following by EOD Friday so we can brief the customer and update the incident?
- Per-route 1h/6h/24h cost and tail-latency heatmaps (time-sliceable).
- Sampled request payloads (anonymized) for the top 20 high-cost flows.
- An anomaly flagging rule and suggested alert thresholds (token rate vs cost-per-token).
- A short runbook: triage steps, ownership handoff, recommended fallback (model variant or cache knob).

I started a draft playbook and attached it (playbook-draft.docx). If product/console folks can own the dashboard slices and sampling plumbing, ops/observability can own the alerting & playbook automation.

Calyx provided a small snippet of their traffic that looks off — they gave us permission to sample. Jordan from Calyx is looped in.

Next steps: can we confirm owners and an ETA for an initial artifact (prototype dashboards + sampling query)? Also any security concerns for sampling (PII filters) — flag them here.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: playbook-draft.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dashboard sweeps + cost-anomaly playbook request

Thanks Aisha — good catch. A couple quick clarifying questions before we scope: 
1) Are the spikes concentrated in generation tokens (streaming responses) or embedding calls? That will change which metrics we prioritize.
2) Do we have sample request_ids for the highest-cost tokens so we can pull full trace/context?

Technical notes / proposal:
- I can own building a per-route time-series widget that shows cost-per-minute and p50/p95 latency; will need a sampling query against our ingest index. I attached the SQL-ish query I usually run (cost-slice-query.sql) — please point me at a few request_ids if available.
- For sampling, we should run privacy filters: drop prompt text beyond first 256 chars, hash any user identifiers, redact emails/phone numbers. Ops should confirm compliance.
- For alerts: propose a rolling 3x cost-per-token increase over baseline with min absolute delta (~$5/hr) to reduce noisy alerts.

ETA: I can put a prototype dashboard together by Wed EOD if Ben can wire the sampling endpoint and Marissa can add the alert rule in Console.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

Attachment: cost-slice-query.sql

Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dashboard sweeps + cost-anomaly playbook request

Looping in ops side detail. We can deliver a lightweight sampling pipeline and an ad-hoc dashboard within the proposed timeline but two practical limits:

1) Storage & retention — full request bodies even sampled will push our short-term retention if we keep raw prompts. I suggest a 7-day short-term store for sampled payloads, then purge. We can persist derived metrics (token_count, model, cost) long-term.
2) Performance — live sampling at peak QPS needs async sinks. I propose writing samples to an S3 bucket via an async worker and indexing only the derived fields into the Console index.

I created a quick mock screenshot of the proposed widget (route-spike-screenshot.png) and opened JIRA: CONSOLE-1427 to track the work. Resource ask: 1 SWE (observability) for 3 sprints + 0.5 SWE part-time to build the short-term storage purge job.

If Calyx needs the raw payloads for their audit, we can provide a redacted export under an NDA. Ops, please confirm.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Observability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: route-spike-screenshot.png
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dashboard sweeps + cost-anomaly playbook request

Thanks for the context and the clear asks. Approve moving forward with the prototype dashboard + sampling pipeline. A few leadership notes: 

- Prioritize guardrails for PII/redaction as non-negotiable. Work with Security on a short checklist before any exported samples leave our systems.
- Include a canary and rollback plan for any alert rules we add to Console (so we avoid noisy paging).
- Schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning (Thu 09:30 PT) to align owners and milestones. Aisha, please invite Jordan from Calyx if they want to observe.

Marissa / Karthik / Ben: please post a brief plan in JIRA CONSOLE-1427 by EOD today with owners, acceptance criteria, and the minimal demo that satisfies Calyx for the incident.

Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
